column1: # rubric.tsv — the sections of the katas warrant set, one per test module, in document order.

column2: The Workstreams: A Directory Is One When It Carries a Queue, Dot-Named Ones Never Are, and the Names Come Back Sorted
The Detached Commit: The mikemol-commit Argv Names Only What Was Asked, and a Log Reads Running, Done or Failed From Its Last rc Line
The Waiter: A Command's Output Then rc=N Lands in Its Log, a Timeout Is Recorded as 124, and the Cleanup Runs Whatever the Result
The Detached Start: The Waiter Argv Carries the Log, the Cleanup Pairs and the Command, and a Started Command's Log Reads Running Then Done
The Fleet: Git State Per Workstream, a Flush That Starts a Detached Commit Only Where the Queue Is Pending and Nothing Is Running, and a Probe That Cleans Up After Itself
The Inbox: Handled Letters Move Into the Archive by Their File Name, a Missing One Is Reported, and an Archived Name Is Never Overwritten
The Hook Survey: A Pre-commit Is Found Where core.hooksPath Says, and It Is Bazel Only When a Non-Comment Line Names Bazel
The Bazel Scaffold: Template Files Are Written With the Repo Name, Never Over an Existing File, and the Hook Is Swapped Only After the Target Passed
The Pulse: The Fleet View Is Status Rows, Then nemik-check's Warnings Minus the Standing Ones, Then the Top of the Ranking
The Host Tick: The Lock Is Taken Under the Holder's Name, and a Tick Closes in Order: Arm, Ledger, Evidence, Flush, Unlock
The Policy File: The Host's Values Are Read From a Data File, Every Missing Required Key Is Named Together, and Nothing Defaults to a Machine
The Command Line: The Host Katas' Subcommand Names Run the Modules, a Delegated One Prints the mtools Command, and a Policy Gap Is Named
